assessment.governing_intent: Make startup reconciliation and listener/dispatch available for current authoritative work without waiting for the full best-effort historical resource cleanup sweep, while preserving historical records, custody checks, resumability, observability, and safety refusals.
implementation_unknowns: The exact current implementation shape of bin/alienintent.mjs, src/runtime/dispatcher.mjs, startupReconcile(), reconcileResources(), listener startup, and resource cleanup code must be inspected before design changes.
The appropriate internal mechanism for bounded cleanup passes, persistence of pending records, and prevention of overlapping cleanup owners must be selected from the existing runtime patterns.
The current #149 claim/listener state and issue #150 body must be read at the specified points because the packet makes them authoritative release/context checks.

The existing test harness and fixtures for retained resources, dirty or mismatched worktrees, live ownership, ambiguous custody, restart behavior, and repeated execution need to be located or created.
The exact form of the feature-regression receipt, candidate branch publication, and independent verification evidence must follow repository/project conventions.
material_risks: Incorrect decoupling could admit current work while weakening ownership, active-claim, supervised-unit, dirty-worktree, or ambiguous-custody protections.
A background or deferred cleanup design could accidentally skip historical cleanup permanently, lose retained records, or become non-resumable after restart.
Concurrency mistakes could allow overlapping cleanup owners or races between listener admission, reconciliation, and cleanup.
Tests that only assert listener startup without proving retained-record survival and later cleanup availability would miss the key safety requirement.
Release procedure requires exact branch/SHA evidence and independent verification; missing evidence could block landing even if the code works.
assessment.next_action: Hand off to one implementation owner to inspect the current issue/repository state, design the bounded resumable cleanup path, implement the focused source and test changes, then publish the candidate SHA and verification evidence as required.
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is READY because material owner intent is resolved: historical cleanup must no longer block current dispatch, but must remain safe, resumable, observable, and non-overlapping. The task does not contain materially independent product or architectural decision centers requiring separate execution, and remaining uncertainty is implementation research rather than owner clarification. External checks are named as part of normal execution/release workflow rather than shown to be unavailable.
assessment.summary: The task defines a cohesive maintenance repair: decouple historical cleanup progress from current admission/dispatch during startup, keep cleanup safe and resumable, and prove the behavior with focused tests and release evidence. The scope boundaries, ownership constraints, non-goals, and acceptance observations are sufficiently specific for autonomous implementation handoff.
assessment.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through discriminating automated tests and release evidence: current eligible work must be admitted while historical cleanup remains pending, retained records must survive restart and repeated execution, dirty or ambiguous/live custody must still refuse, cleanup must be resumable and bounded per pass, and no overlapping cleanup owners may exist. A single independent verification verdict on the candidate SHA is meaningful because the work has one controlling behavioral objective and focused safety invariants.
